Additional Information: Samples were deformed at 77 K, 293 K, and 473 K. Geometric instability (necking) is expected when the work hardening rate is less than the true stress.

Properties.Ultimate Tensile Strength: ru (reduced by more than 40% from 77 K to room temperature)
Properties.Yield Strength: ry (halved at 77 K and reduced with increasing temperature, most significant change between 77 K and room temperature)

Additional Information: Tests performed at temperatures up to 1073 K, with significant changes in yield strength and ultimate tensile strength observed between 77 K and room temperature. Strong temperature dependencies, with maxima occurring at liquid nitrogen temperature.

Properties.Yield Strength: Increases with decreasing temperature (not in early stages of plastic deformation)

Additional Information: Twinning produces high work hardening and increases ultimate tensile strength, but does not explain the increase in yield strength. Increased ductility observed at 77 K may be due to twinning providing an additional deformation mode or inherent solute effect.

Properties.Ultimate Tensile Strength: highest value obtained at liquid nitrogen temperature (77 K)
Properties.Yield Strength: highest value obtained at liquid nitrogen temperature (77 K)

Additional Information: The tensile properties show a monotonic decrease in yield and ultimate tensile strengths with an increase in temperature. The elongations to fracture of all materials also decrease with temperature, except for FG which shows a minimum in ductility at an intermediate temperature.

Tensile tests performed at various temperatures (77, 293, 473, 673, 873, 1073 K) using an Instron 4204 test rig. Tests were conducted in air for room temperature and above, and liquid nitrogen bath was used for tests at 77 K. Additional tensile specimens deformed at test temperatures of 77, 293, and 873 K with interrupted tests at various strain levels.
